cases.root_cause: The function polygonToCellsExperimental writes cells to the output buffer 'out' without knowing its allocated size. The loop at line 713-721 increments 'i' and writes 'out[i++] = iter.cell' for each cell produced by the iterator, but there is no bounds check against the buffer capacity. The caller (fuzzer) allocates an insufficient buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow when the iterator produces more cells than the buffer can hold. The debug-only assertion (H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS_ASSERT) checks against the algorithmic maximum, not the actual buffer size, and is disabled in release builds.

cases.root_cause: In mz_zip_reader_read_central_dir, archive_ofs is computed as eocd_ofs - (cdir_ofs + cdir_size) using unsigned 64-bit arithmetic without checking for underflow. When a crafted ZIP makes eocd_ofs < cdir_ofs + cdir_size, the subtraction wraps to a huge value. This huge archive_ofs is then subtracted from m_archive_size (line 3824), causing m_archive_size to also wrap to a huge value. Later, mz_zip_mem_read_func uses this corrupted m_archive_size for bounds checking, so the check file_ofs >= m_archive_size always passes, allowing reads past the actual memory buffer (m_mem_size).
